body.statement: For a nonzero contrast matrix \(C\), the positive-semidefinite dominance \[\Sigma_C\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}\succeq\Sigma_C(Y)\quad\text{for every }N\text{ divisible by }2K,F,\text{ and }Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)\] holds if and only if all columns of \(C\) vanish except two columns that are negatives of one another. Equivalently, every nonzero universally Loewner-dominated multi-contrast system is a vector rescaling of one pairwise arm contrast. For any other \(C\), there is a direction \(h\) and binary armwise marginals for which common ranking reduces \(\operatorname{Var}_Z(h^{\mathsf T}\widehat\tau)\).
body.justification: Scalar risk optimality does not imply joint covariance conservativeness; this theorem identifies the exact and unexpectedly narrow boundary.
body.gap: No located causal-bootstrap or multi-arm design paper classifies when one completed science table dominates the full covariance matrix for all marginal schedules.
body.consumer: Analysts constructing simultaneous Wald regions learn when a single rank-preserving bootstrap covariance is valid and when contrast-specific completion is unavoidable.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(F\), \(Y\in\mathcal S_N(F)\), and write
\[
 D(Y)=\Sigma_C\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\Sigma_C(Y).
\]
The matrix \(D(Y)\) is symmetric, and therefore \(D(Y)\succeq0\) if and only if \(h^{\mathsf T}D(Y)h\geq0\) for every \(h\in\mathbb R^m\).  For a fixed \(h\), put \(v=C^{\mathsf T}h\).  The scalar estimator \(h^{\mathsf T}\widehat\tau=v^{\mathsf T}\widehat{\bar Y}\) has contrast Gram matrix
\[
 H_h=C^{\mathsf T}hh^{\mathsf T}C=vv^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Moreover, Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}causal\text{-}contrast}\) implies \(v^{\mathsf T}\mathbf 1_K=h^{\mathsf T}C\mathbf 1_K=0\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}cone\text{-}iff}\), applied to the one-dimensional contrast \(h^{\mathsf T}C\), consequently shows that universal Loewner dominance is equivalent to
\[
 v_av_b\leq0\quad\text{for every }a\ne b
 \quad\text{and every }v\in L:=\operatorname{range}(C^{\mathsf T}). \tag{1}
\]

We now classify the linear subspaces \(L\subseteq\mathbf 1_K^{\perp}\) satisfying (1).  Every nonzero \(v\in L\) has at most one positive coordinate and at most one negative coordinate.  Since its coordinates sum to zero, it follows that, for some unordered pair \(\{a,b\}\) and some \(t\ne0\),
\[
 v=t(e_a-e_b). \tag{2}
\]
All nonzero vectors in \(L\) must use the same unordered pair.  Indeed, if \(t(e_a-e_b)\) and \(s(e_c-e_d)\) have disjoint supports, their sum after choosing the signs of \(t,s\) has four nonzero coordinates and violates (1).  If their distinct supports share one coordinate, orienting and scaling them so that the shared coordinate has the same sign produces a linear combination with two coordinates of the opposite common sign, again violating (1).  Thus there is a fixed pair \(\{a,b\}\) such that
\[
 L\subseteq\operatorname{span}(e_a-e_b). \tag{3}
\]
Because \(C\ne0\), equality holds in (3).  Every row of \(C\) is therefore a multiple of \((e_a-e_b)^{\mathsf T}\), so there is a nonzero \(u\in\mathbb R^m\) with
\[
 C=u(e_a-e_b)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Equivalently, column \(a\) is \(u\), column \(b\) is \(-u\), and all other columns vanish.

Conversely, if \(C=u(e_a-e_b)^{\mathsf T}\), then every \(v=C^{\mathsf T}h=(u^{\mathsf T}h)(e_a-e_b)\) satisfies (1).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}cone\text{-}iff}\) gives \(h^{\mathsf T}D(Y)h\geq0\) for every \(h\), every admissible \(F\), and every completion \(Y\), hence \(D(Y)\succeq0\).

Finally, if \(C\) is not of the displayed two-column form, the proved subspace classification supplies \(h\) such that \(v=C^{\mathsf T}h\) has \(v_av_b>0\) for some pair.  The binary construction in the necessity part of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}rank\text{-}cone\text{-}iff}\), with only those two arm marginals nonconstant, then gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_Z\!\left\{h^{\mathsf T}\widehat\tau\mid Y^{\uparrow}(F)\right\}
 -\operatorname{Var}_Z\!\left(h^{\mathsf T}\widehat\tau\mid Y\right)
 =-\frac{v_av_b}{N-1}<0.
\]
This is the required finite binary witness to failure of Loewner dominance.
